## 🎯 Main Idea
- Web reconnaissance: systematically gather information about a website/web app before attacking it.
- Goals: identify assets (domains, subdomains, IPs), uncover hidden info (dirs, files, tech), analyze the attack surface, and gather intelligence (emails, employees, tech stack).
- Uses **active** recon (direct interaction, higher detection risk) and **passive** recon (public data, stealthier / OSINT).

## 💥 Attack / Exploit Vectors
### WHOIS Lookups (passive)
- Query registration data: owner, registrar, dates, nameservers, contacts — useful for social engineering.
- **Commands**
  - `whois example.com` — retrieve domain registration/ownership info

### DNS Enumeration (dig)
- Resolve domains and pull record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA) to map infrastructure.
- **Commands**
  - `dig example.com A` — query the IPv4 A record

### Subdomain Enumeration
- Discover subdomains that expose extra attack surface (dev/staging servers, forgotten apps).
- Active (brute-force, zone transfers) vs passive (CT logs, search engines).
- **Commands**
  - `dnsenum example.com -f subdomains.txt` — dictionary brute-force of subdomains

### DNS Zone Transfers (AXFR)
- Misconfigured DNS servers may hand over the full zone file (all subdomains, IPs, mail config) to any requester.
- **Commands**
  - `dig @ns1.example.com example.com axfr` — request a full zone transfer

### Virtual Host Discovery
- Multiple sites share one IP; brute-force Host headers to reveal hidden vhosts not found by IP scanning.
- **Commands**
  - `gobuster vhost -u http://192.0.2.1 -w hostnames.txt` — enumerate virtual hosts by hostname

### Certificate Transparency (CT) Logs (passive)
- Public SSL/TLS cert logs reveal overlooked subdomains via crt.sh.
- **Commands**
  - `curl -s "https://crt.sh/?q=%25.example.com&output=json" | jq -r '.[].name_value' | sed 's/\*\.//g' | sort -u` — extract unique subdomains from crt.sh

### Fingerprinting
- Identify server software, versions, CMS, frameworks, and WAFs to target known exploits/misconfigs.
- Techniques: banner grabbing, HTTP header analysis, probing for specific responses, page-content analysis.
- **Commands**
  - `curl -I inlanefreight.com` — grab HTTP headers / banner (Server, X-Powered-By)
  - `pip3 install git+https://github.com/EnableSecurity/wafw00f` — install wafw00f
  - `wafw00f inlanefreight.com` — detect presence/type of a WAF
  - `nikto -h inlanefreight.com -Tuning b` — run Nikto software-identification modules only

### Web Crawling / Spidering
- Automated link-following to map site structure and extract links, comments, metadata, and sensitive files (.bak, web.config, logs, keys).
- Breadth-first (broad overview) vs depth-first (reach deep).
- **Commands**
  - `wget -O ReconSpider.zip <htb-url>/ReconSpider.v1.2.zip` — download the custom ReconSpider
  - `python3 ReconSpider.py http://inlanefreight.com` — crawl target, output to results.json
  - `jq -r '.[] | select(.file != null) | .file' example_data.json | sort -u` — extract crawled links

### robots.txt & .well-known URIs
- robots.txt can reveal hidden/off-limits directories.
- `.well-known/` standardized endpoints (security.txt, openid-configuration) expose config/metadata; openid-configuration leaks auth/token/userinfo endpoints and JWKS URI.

### Search Engine Discovery (Google Dorking / OSINT)
- Use advanced operators to find exposed docs, login pages, configs, and directories — passive and legal.
- **Commands**
  - `site:example.com "password reset"` — restrict to a site
  - `inurl:admin login` / `allinurl:admin panel` — term in URL
  - `filetype:pdf "confidential report"` — limit to a file type
  - `intitle:"index of" /backup` — open directory listings
  - `site:example.com inurl:config.php` — hunt config files
  - `cache:example.com` — view cached version

### Web Archives (Wayback Machine)
- Historical snapshots reveal removed pages, old directories, subdomains, and content changes — passive.

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- `whois` — domain registration lookups
- `dig` / `dnsenum` — DNS queries, zone transfers, subdomain brute-force
- `gobuster` (vhost mode) — virtual host enumeration
- `crt.sh` + `jq`/`sed` — CT-log subdomain mining
- `curl -I`, `whatweb`, `Wappalyzer`, `BuiltWith`, `Netcraft`, `Nmap` — fingerprinting
- `wafw00f` — WAF detection
- `Nikto` — web server scanner / fingerprinting
- `Scrapy` / `ReconSpider`, Burp Spider, OWASP ZAP, Apache Nutch — crawlers
- `FinalRecon` — all-in-one recon framework (headers, whois, SSL, crawl, DNS/subdomain/dir enum, wayback, port scan)
  - `./finalrecon.py --headers --whois --url http://inlanefreight.com`
  - `./finalrecon.py --full` / `--ps` / `--wayback`
- Google Dorks, Wayback Machine — OSINT / passive recon

## 🛡️ Mitigations
- Restrict DNS zone transfers to authorized secondary servers only.
- Suppress/obfuscate verbose banners and version headers; add security headers (HSTS).
- Use domain privacy services to mask WHOIS data.
- Remove sensitive/backup/config files from web roots and restrict directory listing.
